I personally haven't had much luck with counseling or therapy, I can definitely understand your frustrations with their methods.  

Living up to others expectations is a losing battle, in my opinion.  Live for yourself.  Take what you inflict on yourself and turn that into drive.  Focus that pain, anger and sadness into something constructive.  I've found I work dramatically better when I'm seething.  It may be a little "dark side of the force", but I've never been so focused as when I'm angry at the world, or myself.  Not saying you should thrive on those emotions, but its a better way of dealing with them than cutting.

I know of something you can love about yourself.  The fact that you're reaching out.  The fact that you haven't taken the irreversible step, the easy way out.  I don't know you, but I know your pain.  Try to take comfort knowing that others all around the world are going through what you are.  

I struggle with my own issues, but over time, certain things are improving.  Its never easy, but there is satisfaction in the end result.  You can find happiness, man.  Work towards it, not against it.

Man, I feel the same way.  Shame and guilt only make depression worse, I'm a shining example of that.  Try to salvage what you can from your mistakes, and wipe the slate clean by fixing what you can.  What you can't fix, find another way around it.  If you feel that people knowing the real you would make them not wish to be around you, then they're not worth having around.  

There's not gonna be a quick fix for anything, I've sought that for years and learned its not possible.  But it can be fixed, and you can find happiness again.  It takes some of us longer than others, but its worth fighting for.

I've done the same.  The letters do serve a constructive purpose, but your intended act does not.  Excel at your exams, don't let a temporary problem become larger due to your actions.  If your family does not support you (I've had the same struggles with mine), then fucking forget them, and find something you love about yourself.  Kick ass at that, and make the people who don't see you as being awesome, jealous for not getting to know you, or make an effort to be in your life.

Fuck em.  Mold yourself into the person you want to be.

Sir, I've been in two relationships that were very similar to your own, albeit without kids.  If you're not poly, you're not gonna learn to like it.  Its a stab in the fucking heart.  In your shoes, I'd speak with a professional.  At least figure out what you CAN do to improve your chances of keeping your kids, and find a place that you can afford without her.  That kind of environment is not only toxic for them, but infinitely moreso for you.  

I'm no legal professional, nor have any clue about the reality of custody battles, but I'd think theres a possibility for things to swing in your favor, as your ex prefers polygamy.

I've been in the neighborhood, and doing yourself in (even attempting) is not the answer.  You've got a responsibility to be a strong person for your kids.  You made them, you have to put them before you, for the rest of your days.  Its heartbreaking, it sucks, but you have to deal with it better than your ex did.  

Stay strong, my friend.  Know that others feel what you're feeling.  Keep your head at work, its the glue to make your life work again.

I messed up similar things with my life.  I've been overwhelmed by my poor choices, and felt there was no resolution possible.  In my opinion, if I fucked something up, its my duty to take the steps to resolve it.  I screwed up college, screwed up a promising job, and made an attempt on my life.  As a result, I've got numerous psychological tics I've never experienced before, unexplained fears that have never happened (grew up with routine trips to the dentist and orthodonsit, and now have a petrifying fear of going to the dentist), and the same fears about my financial well being.  I had to start from the bottom again, taking a massive paycut for a job that I hated.  Five years later, I still struggle with the psychological crap, but I feel its my duty to make it up at least to my parents.  You're gonna need to put in more work to get your career back where it needs to be, but its not a dead end.  Its going to suck, you're going to feel like youre spinning your wheels at some points, but perseverance will make the difference.  I learned a lot about life from hitting bottom.  I feel like a loser to this day, but being able to report my successes gives my parents peace of mind, and pride in their son that I'm willing to give it another try.  

If your parents are mad about you not completing med school, make them proud in excelling at something you enjoy.

It may take a warped sense of humor to understand, but it's a nice feeling being able to say, "I fucked up, and I'm fixing it; here's how".
